memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron to give him dignity and honor. Tell all the skilled workers to whom I have given wisdom in such matters that they are to make garments for Aaron, for his consecration, so he may serve me as priest." - Exodus 28:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives a striking reason for the priestly garments: to give Aaron dignity and honour. The clothing was not for Aaron's vanity but to reflect the weight and beauty of the office he held. When he stood before the people in those robes, they saw something of the seriousness of approaching God.

Notice too who makes them — skilled workers "to whom I have given wisdom in such matters." God takes credit for their craftsmanship. Their ability to weave, embroider, and set stones was itself a gift from Him. Practical skill is not separate from spiritual gifting; God distributes both, and both can serve His purposes.

There is dignity here for everyone reading. God is a God who clothes people with honour. Isaiah rejoiced that God had clothed him with garments of salvation and arrayed him in a robe of righteousness (Isa 61:10). In Christ, you have been given something far greater than Aaron's robes — His own righteousness covering you. Whatever the world says about your status or worth, God has dressed you in dignity. And whatever skill sits in your hands, He gave it, and He can use it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I recognise my practical skills as gifts God has given me?
Do I live conscious of the dignity God has clothed me with in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You clothe Your people with dignity and honour. Thank You for the righteousness of Christ covering me. Help me use the skills You have given for Your purposes. Amen.
